resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy for Sale (resale certificate)
resale_co.issued_by: City of South Amboy Building Department
requirements: Full property maintenance inspection; the resale certificate is not issued unless the property is 100% compliant
Address numbers visible from the street; yard free of weeds and debris
Clear path to the electrical panel; all outlets, switches and junction boxes covered; no extension cords as permanent wiring
Combustibles at least 3 feet from furnace and water heater; access to the furnace room
Water heater with cold water shut-off and pressure relief valve with down spout; gas shut-off on gas heaters
Windows open easily and stay open; no cracked or broken glass; screens on door windows used for ventilation
Handrail on stairs more than 3 risers high; guardrails on open stairs, landings or balconies over 30 inches
Appliances and plumbing fixtures properly installed and working
Working smoke detector on each level including the basement; CO detector near all bedrooms
Work done without required permits must be permitted and all open permits finaled (fines up to $2,000 per week)
All utilities on at the time of inspection
Solid core door between garage and living area
Fire extinguisher (at least 2.5 lb.) mounted in the kitchen area (as printed on the City guideline sheet)
resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the City's 'Certificate of Occupancy for Sale' form (property, seller, buyer, estimated closing date, and the attorney holding escrow for outstanding municipal charges) and return it to the Building Department, 140 North Broadway, South Amboy, NJ 08879 (phone 732-525-5927, fax 732-727-6139). The application fee line on the form is filled in by the City; no amount is printed.

resale_co.notes: The City's Forms page (loaded from the site's forms data) lists 'Certificate of Occupancy for Sale' under Building. The 4-page PDF is a scan (read visually): page 1 is the application, page 2 a 'Fire Code' sheet on smoke detectors, CO alarms and fire extinguishers, page 3 the Housing Inspection Guidelines, and page 4 the Tax/Utility Collector's final sewer instructions. No fee amount, lead time or validity period is printed, and the City code (ecode360 SO0670) could not be opened. Search engine summaries mentioned a $50 fee for South Amboy but no official source showing the words was found, so no fee is recorded. No named Building Department contact was found on the City site; the Building Department email is not displayed on the site. The City also runs rental housing inspections (732-525-5936), which are not a resale item. The guideline sheet's fire extinguisher line is undated and may predate P.L.2025, c.19.

requirements: City 'Fire Code' sheet (undated, in the CO for Sale packet): 10-year sealed battery smoke detector on each level including the basement, unless the home has original A/C powered single or multiple-station alarms
Smoke detectors in every separate sleeping area within 10 feet of each bedroom door; a loft or attic used as living space with 7 feet or more headroom often needs one
CO alarm near sleeping areas; combination smoke/CO units must be 10-year sealed battery units
Homes with a monitored alarm system: the owner must be able to give the alarm company name and silence and reset the alarm after the test

County Fire Marshal sheet: smoke alarms no older than 10 years; CO alarms no older than 5 years (or the maker's date); detector type depends on the year built (1990 and later: electric with battery backup, all interconnected, one in each bedroom); house numbers at least 4 inches; certificate valid 6 months

The same undated sheet lists fire extinguisher rules (2A-10B:C, 10 lb. or less, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor, serviced or bought within 12 months); P.L.2025, c.19 removed the state extinguisher requirement, so confirm whether this still applies

fire_cert.notes: The DCA July 2026 registry lists the County (code C) as South Amboy's fire enforcing agency, and the City's Fire Prevention page says all fire prevention services are provided by the Middlesex County Fire Marshal. The County's web pages returned 403 Forbidden to plain requests. The fee schedule used here is the County Fire Marshal's own letter to 'All Real Estate Agencies/Home Owners' (citing County Fire Marshal Ordinance 10-1811), found as a scanned PDF on the South River Borough site (created February 2026; letter undated). It is the County's schedule, not a South River fee, but South Amboy does not post it, so confirm it applies. An older County form (2020, Internet Archive copy of http://www.middlesexcountynj.gov/Government/Departments/PSH/Documents/Fire-Marshal/Residential Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Inspection Info and Application.pdf) also showed a $50 fee. The City page's Fire Marshal email is hidden behind email protection and was not decoded; the Fire Official's email comes from the state directory. Type is 'unknown' because the schema has no county option. The City's CO for Sale packet also includes a 'Fire Code' sheet, so the Building Department's resale inspection may check alarms too. Oddity: the state directory's smoke detector compliance block on the Sayreville page names 'City of South Amboy Hg/Code Enf' at 140 N Broadway, while South Amboy's own page names the County Fire Marshal.

other_items.label: Final sewer bill
other_items.detail: If a final bill is needed for a closing, first final the water with Middlesex Water (732-634-1500), then send a copy of the final water bill with the attorney or title company contact to the Tax/Utility Collector (Joanne Katko, 732-525-5924); the final sewer takes 5 business days once all information is in.

other_items.label: Outstanding municipal charges
other_items.detail: The CO for Sale form asks for the attorney holding escrow for outstanding municipal charges (tax or sewer).

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: Work done without required permits must be permitted, and any outstanding permits must have final approvals.
